chapter_name: Arts of the People, With the People, For the People
learning_objective: 🎯 Journey into the heart of India to discover beautiful folk arts and traditional crafts created by everyday communities!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Folk art is not created in fancy studios. It is beautiful art made by ordinary village communities, like Warli or Madhubani paintings, passed down through generations from grandparents to children.
Traditional artists use simple motifs like geometric animals, blooming flowers, and dancing figures to tell rich stories about nature, festivals, and their daily village life.
Folk art is a team effort! It brings the whole community together during festivals to paint the walls of their homes, weave vibrant textiles, and celebrate their shared history.

fun_activity.title: 🌺 The Warli Wall Masterpiece
fun_activity.instructions: Use a white crayon or pen on a piece of brown paper to draw a small village scene in the Warli style, using only basic triangles, circles, and straight lines for the people and animals!

quick_recap: ⭐ Folk art is deeply rooted in the daily lives, traditions, and celebrations of local communities.
⭐ Indigenous artists use bold, simple motifs to tell complex stories about their deep connection with nature.
⭐ Creating and sharing traditional crafts keeps our rich cultural heritage alive for the future generations.
